correctness.rationale: Exact coordinate identity t²(u+v+w)+uvw gives a nonsquare function in k(P²), hence first purely inseparable degree two. Differentiation gives the three target cubics; their algebraic-closure base locus is exactly seven reduced Fano-plane points with full cotangent rank. Their complete blowup anticanonical net has square two and dominant image, forcing degree two; Jacobian wedge vanishes, proving pure inseparability. The two field extensions compose to degree four. The classical primitive integer quartic polynomial reduces to the fourth power of the dual plane. Full proof and verified symbolic certificates are in RESULT.md and verify.py; finite F2 enumeration is supplemented by an algebraic-closure proof.

value.rationale: The nonordinary characteristic-two duality degeneration of a canonical four-nodal cubic is described structurally, not just by polynomial reduction: the seven distinguished Fano-plane centers give an anticanonical net of self-intersection two and the Gauss map admits two natural purely inseparable double stages. The distinction between reduced Gauss dual and flat quartic specialization is geometrically motivated, and its precise geometric explanation is useful in inseparable duality and weak del Pezzo surface constructions.
